Cinematic Editor Mason About

Two tools for 1.8.9

A camera and replay editor for filming, and a visual world editor for building. Free, open source, and written from scratch for a version everyone else stopped supporting.

Early and largely untested. Both mods were built for one person's own use. They compile and each release was reasoned through carefully, but most of the behaviour has never been verified in a running game. Expect rough edges, and back up any world you care about before using Mason.

Cinematic Editor

v1.24.0

Fly a camera along a keyframed path, record a fight and replay it as ghosts so you can frame the shot after it happened, grade the picture with a library of effects, and export the result as video. Client-side only — nothing is sent to the server.

  • Detached camera

    Driven by a client-only entity, so your player never moves and the server sees nothing. Physical fly and walk modes are there when you want to be in shot.

  • Keyframed paths

    Position, rotation and field of view on independent tracks, along Catmull-Rom splines with per-side easing.

  • Replay

    Records every player once a tick, with their skins, armour, held items, swings and hit reactions. Runs on the timeline clock or one of its own.

  • Tracking & follow

    Aim at a chosen player with a blendable weight, ride along at a set distance, or generate a perfect orbit around anything.

  • 37 effects

    Grading, bloom, anamorphic streaks, lens flare, motion trails, painterly, outline, grain, FXAA. Every one of them keyframable.

  • Subject masking

    Any shader effect can be limited to one person, or to everything except them — monochrome world, subject in colour.

  • World capture

    Writes the terrain of a fight into a new save, so a replay carries its own world and can be reframed months later.

  • Video export

    PNG sequence or straight into ffmpeg. Fixed timestep, so a slow encoder makes the export longer rather than dropping frames.

KeyAction
F8Open the editor
F7Toggle the free camera
F9Add a keyframe
F6Start / stop recording players
F10Play / stop the timeline
F4Enable / disable the whole mod

Mason

v0.8.0

Visual world editing: selections you can see, weighted block palettes, region operations, terrain brushes, a clipboard with rotation, portable schematics and undo. Roughly what a world editor gives you, with a panel instead of a command line.

Singleplayer only. A hard limit rather than a missing feature — a client mod cannot edit a server's world. Everything here writes through the integrated server, which only exists when you are the one hosting.

  • Visible selections

    Two corners set from anywhere you can see, not just within reach. Box, sphere or cylinder, each drawn as its own outline, through walls.

  • Weighted palettes

    70% stone, 20% cobble, 10% andesite reads as rock. One block reads as one block.

  • Block browser

    Every block state in the game, searchable and sorted, named the way the creative menu names them - air included, so you can fill only the gaps.

  • Region operations

    Fill, erase, replace, cut one material to air, hollow, walls, shell and stack — all following the selected shape.

  • Brushes

    Paint, erase, replace, surface coat, and a top-layer mode that follows a hillside instead of painting a flat disc across it. Width, height and angle set separately, and every brush can be clipped to the selection.

  • Terrain sculpting

    A Gaussian smooth over the surface height map, flatten toward the height you clicked, and carve or raise a soft-edged dome, all at a strength you set.

  • Clipboard

    Copy, paste, rotate and flip, with stairs and doors turning along with the build.

  • Schematics

    Save a build to disk and paste it into a different world. Stored by block name, so it survives a different mod list.

  • Undo

    24 steps, up to two million changed blocks each. One brush stroke is one step.

KeyAction
BEnter / leave editor mode
NOpen the panel
VArm / disarm the brush
] / [Bigger / smaller brush
Z / XSet corner 1 / corner 2
